questions.question: What did the customer say about support quality and the mobile app?
questions.expected_answer: The customer rated support quality as good and described the mobile app as dated.
questions.author: reviewer

questions.question: How exposed is Larkspur to its single biggest customer?
questions.expected_answer: The largest single customer accounts for 9% of revenue.
questions.author: reviewer

questions.question: Which EBITDA figure should we use for the base case, given the latest diligence?
questions.expected_answer: The restated CIM gives EUR 24m; the draft QoE gives EUR 21.5m after excluding EUR 2.5m of planned savings that have not started.
questions.author: reviewer

questions.question: Does the retention evidence clear the 105% hurdle once the one-off bundle is removed?
questions.expected_answer: Management reports 112%; the cohort analysis gives 104% excluding the bundle and 111% including it, so the result depends on the measurement basis.
questions.author: reviewer

questions.question: How did the recurring-revenue mix move when the second CIM was issued?
questions.expected_answer: It moved from 78% in CIM v1 to 80% in CIM v2; the later QoE reports 71% under its fee classification.
questions.author: reviewer

questions.question: Between the first and restated CIM, did Larkspur change its headquarters or customer-base description?
questions.expected_answer: No material change is reported: it remains headquartered in Amsterdam and serves about 1,400 fleet operators.
questions.author: reviewer

questions.question: What proportion of next year's customer renewals is at risk?
questions.expected_answer: The documents do not provide a renewal schedule or the share of next year's renewals at risk.

questions.expected_answer: The documents do not state year-end net working capital.
